metadata.title: HVS7: a chemically peculiar hyper-velocity star

evidence.quote: HVS 7: a chemically peculiar hyper-velocity star

SDSS J113312.12+010824.9(aka HVS 7, Brown et al.
2006) is the 4th-brightest HVS candidate known (V = 17.80).

The evolutionary status and GC origin of the hyper-velocity star SDSS J113312.12+010824.9 (aka HVS 7) is constrained from
a detailed study of its stellar parameters and chemical composition.
The spectroscopic distance is then 59±6 kpc, in excellent agreement with the distance estimate of Brown et al. (2006).

notes: HVS 7 (= SDSS J113312.12+010824.9) is included as a follow-up target: T:p1-b15 calls it the already-known "4th-brightest HVS candidate known" from Brown et al. (2006), while the paper's quantitative study does not establish a GC origin and defers that test to Gaia (T:p4-b7).

SDSS J113312.12+010824.9: The paper reports no explicit RA, Dec, parallax, radial-velocity value, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability. The proper-motion components and ∼830 km/s space velocity in T:p4-b7 are predictions for an assumed Galactic-centre origin, not measured astrometry. The object designation contains coordinate-like text, but it is not treated as an explicit reported position.
